posts.author: BobH
posts.content_md:
I believe I just bought the last new Metrologic Sandbox Holography Kit. I saw one offered on Ebay recently, and did a search for them on the web. Metrologic no longer has them available, but the search turned up a surplus electronics place that apparently bought up all of their old stock. Two were available, but I didn't buy then because I'm a procrastinator.

Anyway, I decided this morning to check it out again, and *one* was left! Not any more! 

This kit started many holographers on their career paths.

posts.author: tpark
posts.content_md:
I bought a couple of these kits a while ago for parts and odds and ends. There is a bunch of good stuff in the kit (I used the filter pieces for making the safelight). It comes with a rather noisy transmission hologram of a skull, plus a manual on how to make holograms. The film that was in the package was ancient, so I didn't use it. 

I use a hard table, so the pvc tubing mounted items weren't useful to me.

posts.author: JohnFP
posts.content_md: Bob, that was my first starter kit. Brings back memories.

posts.author: lucaslab
posts.content_md:
I have bought this kit and I'm very impressed.

It contains:

2 lenses for the laser beam,

2 mirrors,

1 splitter,

1 curved mirror for making cylindrical holograms,

films,

a very good manual,

several other items for helping making holograms.

Also the prize is very affordable for what it includes.

I purchased it because it was the only kit that you could make cylindrical holograms , but the other items proved very useful even for holograms in films or plates as we know them.

Especially the manual has all the technices that are available for reflection or transmission holograms.

I believe that your buy of the kit worths every cent that you spend.

posts.author: BobH
posts.content_md:
I received the kit today, and I'm glad to see that the box is in great condition. The manual is based on T. Jeong's "A Study Guide on Holography" (a draft of which is also in my collection) and appears to be very complete. The transmission hologram included with the kit is a very noisy image of a human skull (what else ), and the beamsplitter is missing. The jar for making cylindrical holograms is plastic (wasn't it originally glass?). Despite these things, I'm very happy to have the kit and think it would have been easily worth the money for someone starting out as a hobbiest. Especially if they had *some* experience developing photographs before they tried holography. 

If anyone has an original beamsplitter that came with the kit, I'd be happy to trade a hologram or some other optic for it. I'd like to have the kit complete for my collection, and promise you'll be happy with the trade!

posts.author: tpark
posts.content_md: It was just a hunk of window glass from what I could tell - nothing fancy at all. Look for something that looks like a small hunk of rectangular window in one of the envelopes. If it's still missing, I'll have a look and I'll send you mine if I can find it, for what it's worth.

posts.author: BobH
posts.content_md:
Apparently I spoke too soon in my excitement...Metrologic Kits are still available. I just came across more of these kits for sale at anchoroptical dot com (an offshoot of Edmund). 

While you're there, check out the spectrometer for 24.95! I've had one for years and they're great. You can use it to measure the color and spectral bandwidth of your Reflection holograms accurately to the nM. Well worth the money, and a great demo thing for kids!
